question: Should `claws apply --yes` count as ClawHub review-required risk acknowledgement for skill artifacts, or must Claw apply require a separate explicit acknowledgement/prompt?
rationale: The existing ClawHub skill installer treats review-required releases as a separate trust decision, and this PR changes that boundary for manifests without maintainer-confirmed policy.

options.title: Require explicit risk acknowledgement
options.body: Fail closed or prompt unless Claw apply receives a dedicated risk acknowledgement option, with tests for clean, review-required, and blocked releases.

options.title: Treat `--yes` as sufficient
options.body: Allow the broad apply confirmation to accept ClawHub review-required skill risk, but document and test that security-policy choice explicitly.

options.title: Limit initial support
options.body: Only install clean or official ClawHub skill artifacts through Claw apply until the broader trust UX is resolved.

recommendation.title: Require explicit risk acknowledgement
recommendation.body: Fail closed or prompt unless Claw apply receives a dedicated risk acknowledgement option, with tests for clean, review-required, and blocked releases.

likelyOwner.reason: The risk acknowledgement contract is currently owned by the ClawHub install-trust path attributed to this recent history.
